name: Somalia

findings.controller: HMN Tech (formerly Huawei Marine); cable owned by PEACE Cable International Network Co. (Hengtong Group)
findings.local_actor: SOMCABLE and MSG Group (Hargeisa-based landing partners)
findings.summary: The PEACE submarine cable, supplied by HMN Tech and owned by a Hengtong Group subsidiary, was reported landed at Berbera in Somaliland, with Hargeisa firms SOMCABLE and MSG Group as local landing partners.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: HMN Tech supplied the system and a PRC firm owns it. Scale subnational because the landing serves Somaliland, a self-declared state the federal government does not control; reviewer may prefer national. Tier 4: landing reported, ready-for-service date in Berbera not stated. Single opened source, so not corroborated.

findings.local_actor: Djibouti Telecom and unnamed Somali partners
findings.summary: The DARE submarine cable from Djibouti to Mombasa, supplied by TE SubCom under a contract in force, was planned with branches landing at Mogadishu, Berbera and Bosaso; construction was reported underway.
findings.analyst_inference: SubCom is US-headquartered, so pole us. Tier 3 on a supply contract in force; later service status not verified in this run, so still_current null and the pre-2020 date applies. Somali landing partner not named in the source (Somtel suspected, unconfirmed). Single opened source.

findings.summary: Somalia's National Communications Authority granted Starlink an operating licence at a Mogadishu ceremony, saying the satellite service would expand national and rural internet access and soon be available nationwide.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 as licence issued; scale and uptake of service not verified. Lead brief said 2024; sources date the licence to April 2025. Whether the licence is honoured in Somaliland is not addressed. Both opened reports likely trace to the same NCA announcement.

findings.controller: Federal Government of Somalia (Ministry of Communications and Technology)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communications and Technology; National Communications Authority
findings.summary: The federal communications minister marked the start of construction of a government national data centre in Mogadishu; builder, financier, equipment vendor and value were not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Mechanically corroborated (NCA S1 + Construct Africa), but confidence lowered: an August 2026 Dawan report describes a national data centre as still being planned, so the 2023 groundbreaking may have stalled or the projects differ. Not AI-specific. An August 2024 ministerial visit to a Beijing data centre (MoCT, opened) produced no reported agreement and is not coded.

findings.builder: Vertiv (US) with distributor Pure Earth International
findings.summary: Vertiv completed power and cooling installation for Hormuud Telecom's open-access cable landing station in Somalia, intended to host several submarine cables; location and connected cables not disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator Hormuud is Somali, so domestic; Vertiv supplied facility power/cooling, not network equipment, so recorded as builder. Tier 5 judged from completion; operational use not confirmed. Single opened source, so not corroborated. Low strategic weight.
